claim: Written abatement application to the assessors must be filed within 185 days from commitment; assessors may also abate on their own initiative within one year.
After one year but within 3 years from commitment, the municipal officers may abate for illegality, error or irregularity, but may not grant an abatement to correct an error in valuation.
If a municipality has a board of assessment review, an applicant denied abatement may appeal in writing to it within 60 days after notice of the decision or deemed denial.

Residential appeals from the board of assessment review go directly to Superior Court under Rule 80B; nonresidential property or property with equalized municipal valuation of $1,000,000 or greater goes to the State Board of Property Tax Review within 60 days.
A taxpayer filing an appeal must pay the greater of the prior year's taxes (up to current taxes due) or the undisputed current taxes; this does not apply to property valued under $500,000.
'Certified ratio' is the level of assessed value, as a percentage of just value, as certified by the assessor under 36 M.R.S. §383.
